extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers interested in postwar politics, labor and economic policy
extracted.subtask_description: A newspaper article reporting speeches, negotiations and policy proposals about postwar domestic and economic policy, labor-management relations, and government action. Covers proposals by politicians, Senate secrecy on atomic matters, and union–management bargaining developments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Over-all objective of the American system
rubrics_metrics.description: The over-all objective of the American system in the years ahead should be to furnish to all the men and women and children of America all of the necessities, and to an increasing degree the comforts of modern life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implement policies that supply necessities and growing comforts for the population; view economic policy in light of providing broad material welfare and progress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Place opportunity above security
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitively placing opportunity above security on our list of priorities; encourage and applaud the pioneer—the originator—the inventor—the adventurer—the risk taker.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid becoming a nation of security seekers; prioritize policies that foster entrepreneurship, new businesses and risk-taking as engines of job creation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support making of profits while opposing abuses
rubrics_metrics.description: We must all of us, business and labor and government, look upon the making of profits with approval. Profits are the ignition system that makes our economic machine operate ... There must be a vigorous opposition to excess profits from monopolies, from unfair practices, from suppression of wages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize profits as necessary for production and jobs, but resist monopolistic or abusive profit-taking; balance pride in company success with safeguards against exploitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Support strong unions but guard against abuses
rubrics_metrics.description: Likewise, we must all of us, capital and management, government and labor, alike, support strong unions. This does not mean that we should condone abuses in unions. There should be an increasing safeguarding of the rights of the individual workmen. There should be increasing democracy and financial accounting in some unions now autocratically run, with periodic choice of their officers by secret ballot. There should be increased discipline within the ranks of some unions. There must be an effective insistence upon respect for contracts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage robust unions as part of checks and balances in private capitalism while promoting internal union democracy, financial accountability, discipline, and respect for contracts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to strike preserved but narrowly used
rubrics_metrics.description: The right to strike must be maintained. ... But the right to strike should be very rarely used. It should be like the right to shoot in self-defense. It should be recognized by both labor and management that all disputes must be settled some time, and that all are so much better off if settlement is made first while production continues.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protect strike rights legally, but promote norms and mechanisms to minimize strikes and favor settlements that keep production ongoing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extend unemployment and old-age insurance carefully
rubrics_metrics.description: Unemployment compensation should be promptly extended in its coverage and in its adequacy both as to amount and as to duration. The same is true of old age and survivor’s insurance. But government must carefully analyze the amount of unemployment compensation and justly administer the system so that it does not in practice actually encourage idleness when jobs are available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Broaden and strengthen social insurance while designing benefits and administration to avoid perverse work-disincentive effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right of business to manage its affairs
rubrics_metrics.description: The right of business to manage its affairs must be vigorously defended. Foremen and other supervisory personnel should be under the unquestioned, exclusive direction of management and not of labor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Affirm managerial authority over operational control and supervision; maintain clear lines of managerial prerogative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Companies must provide more information to labor and public
rubrics_metrics.description: There must be an increasing safeguarding of the rights of the individual. The companies must adjust the conduct of their businesses to a greater amount of information to labor and to the public. It does not add up to say... that high productivity should be a major concern of labor, and in the next breath say that it’s none of labor’s business what are the profits of its company.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage transparency of company financial facts to workers and the public to foster informed labor–management dialogue; management also entitled to inform employees on subjects—consider Wagner Act changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repeal restrictive Wagner Act provisions (management right to inform)
rubrics_metrics.description: The restrictive provision of the Wagner act in this respect should be repealed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Modify labor law to allow management broader rights to inform employees during labor relations, balancing with protections for workers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government corrective action should be minimal and targeted
rubrics_metrics.description: Government should step into each problem or abuse and take action, but its action should be to correct the abuse with the very minimum of exercise of its own powers, to provide necessary limits for the action of its citizens and to avoid detailed regulation of every business or of every citizen.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adopt a limited-government approach: intervene to correct abuses but avoid over-regulation and excessive governmental control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government projects should use private capital and not compete with private enterprise
rubrics_metrics.description: These plans should be carried out by contracts, with the use of private capital and individual enterprise, and not by governmental pay rolls. Government projects must be of a nature that do not primarily compete with private enterprise but stimulate it and open up availabilities for further private investment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer public–private contracting and projects that complement rather than crowd out private businesses; seek self-supporting, self-liquidating projects when possible.

rubrics_metrics.name: Modernize cities and national infrastructure
rubrics_metrics.description: Modernizing our cities with major increases in traffic arteries, clearing out blighted city areas and making them available for rebuilding and redeveloping by private capital, constructing a nation-wide and hemispheric network of highways, increased air facilities, new hospital facilities and expanded educational plants, are but a few potentialities of governmental activity of a useful nature for the people.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use government to enable large-scale infrastructure and urban redevelopment projects that facilitate private redevelopment and broader economic activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobilize semi-stagnant pools of capital
rubrics_metrics.description: Semi-stagnant pools of capital must be vigorously avoided or countered. A conservative portion of the vast resources of the insurance companies of the nation ... must be used in an increasingly vigorous and stimulating manner. Commercial banks must be encouraged to temper the super-caution that followed the banking disasters of 1932.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encourage use of institutional capital (insurance funds, banks) for productive investment rather than hoarding; policy measures or incentives may be needed to mobilize such capital.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defend private capital and avoid concentration of power
rubrics_metrics.description: The private capital aspect of our system should likewise be vigorously defended. ... Much better that there be a wide diversity of private owners than that the power of capital be added to the other powers of government. The concentration of power in any hands under any circumstances is a danger.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promote diverse private ownership to prevent concentration of economic power and safeguard liberty; resist nationalization of industry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Broadly spread the tax burden to maintain confidence
rubrics_metrics.description: The confidence of the people as a whole in the management of the huge war-time debt must be maintained at a high level. This can best be done by frankly telling the people as a whole that the soundest way to maintain the private enterprise system and have it be vigorous and indebtedness, is to broadly spread the tax burden. All must carry a share of the cost of the debt burden and of government spending.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use transparent fiscal policy and broad-based taxation sharing the burden to preserve public confidence in debt management and private enterprise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Develop ways to move capital and labor quickly
rubrics_metrics.description: We need better ways to quickly move capital and labor from place to place in the shifting economic scene. There is a continuing obligation on the worker to search for jobs, to move to jobs, to train for jobs, and then to produce on the jobs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Facilitate labor and capital mobility through training, relocation support and incentives so the economy can adjust dynamically to changing needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use productive manpower via imaginative, wide-scope projects
rubrics_metrics.description: Government must be prepared to currently utilize to the maximum feasible degree the productive man power of the country that is not absorbed by other economic activity. In other words, extensive plans of wide scope and imagination of projects that will be useful to the people should be constantly available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain ready public plans that can absorb unused productive capacity by contracting with private enterprise for useful projects rather than creating artificial work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ten-year test of the American system
rubrics_metrics.description: Let us all agree upon a thorough ten-year test. Let us begin promptly to join together—government, labor, business and agriculture—and to do everything possible to champion and encourage and develop the basic American system. At the end of ten years of united vigorous support let us observe the result, while we then make our decisions as to future policies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commit to a decade-long coordinated national effort to support private capital, individual enterprise and free workmen, then evaluate outcomes before making major structural changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prompt bipartisan 60-day economic conference with public transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: A prompt conference should be called including leadership in its formulation particularly at a time 'when the scarcity of supply makes it necessary.' It should include management, labor, agriculture, top economists and representation from both political parties; these conferences should be carried on with a maximum of public information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Create an authoritative, bipartisan body for wages, prices and production policy with broad membership and public reporting to build confidence and input from rank-and-file economic groups.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sixty-day conference: suspend strikes and make solutions retroactive
rubrics_metrics.description: During a sixty-day period while this conference meets, labor should be requested to discontinue all present strikes, to renew the no-strike pledge, and to set about producing the great multitude of products which we so urgently need. The understanding should be that the solutions arrived at after this conference is held will be retroactive to the beginning of any strikes now being conducted or to the end of the contracts that expired, as the case may be.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use a time-limited truce to allow an authoritative conference to negotiate solutions, with agreed retroactivity to protect workers and production continuity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary government price control when necessary
rubrics_metrics.description: There must also be a temporary government price control in place of competitive price control. To fail to exercise that leadership and foresight means that the policy is formed in a violent clash between economic forces resulting in great damage to the entire economic system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When scarcity threatens stability, employ temporary price controls as a leadership measure to prevent destructive pricing competition and economic clashes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide judicial tribunals with power (jurisdictional disputes)
rubrics_metrics.description: Government must provide judicial tribunals with the power decisions for the ... of jurisdictional dis[putes].
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strengthen judicial or adjudicative mechanisms to resolve jurisdictional labor or economic disputes—grant necessary authority to tribunals (text fragmented in source).

rubrics_metrics.name: Study and publish best company labor-practice examples
rubrics_metrics.description: A study should be made of the 100 companies in America that have had the most successful labor relations and production records in the last ten years. The results of this study should be published throughout the country.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and disseminate best practices from top-performing companies to promote better labor relations and productivity nationwide.

rubrics_metrics.name: Government leadership but broad-based confidence in recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Government in a democracy should not decree such a policy. But it should take a leadership role in the formulation. This is particularly true when scarcity of supply makes it necessary, and the responsibility to be constructive rests with equal weight upon the minority party and the majority party under the American political system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Government should provide leadership and help coordinate policy formulation while ensuring bipartisan participation to secure public confidence.
